To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consuming foods perceived as high in fat may have a negative impact on food reward.
the perceived low fat content of a food is associated with increased food reward and this is moderated by cognitive restraint.
The perception that a popular Brazilian food is 'healthy or 'low fat has been proposed as a key issue influencing eating behaviour and food reward.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how people perceive food, the impact this has on their food choices and the subsequent impact on food intake.
how people perceive the healthiness of food and how this impacts on food reward and food choice.
how people perceive food and how these perceptions influence eating behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the perceived health value (fat content) of two popular foods was confirmed and that consuming a food perceived as 'high fat' had a greater impact on implicit wanting than a food perceived as low fat.

consuming foods perceived to contain less fat (e.g. a low-fat chicken sandwich) may result in increased implicit wanting for food that is perceived to contain higher amounts of fat (e.g high fat chocolate cake).
consuming foods that are perceived as low in fat can increase food reward and this effect can be moderated by restrained eating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perception of food healthiness is an important factor in the food choice and eating behaviour and that the perception of the food healthiness is influenced by the individual eating behaviours.
the perception that a food was 'low fat' had a positive impact on subsequent food reward in individuals with low cognitive restraint.
the consumption of foods that are perceived to be low in fat can increase subsequent food reward and this is moderated by the cognitive restraint eating style.
The main takeaway from our work is that
food marketing and food perception is a very powerful tool that should be considered in the context of the obesity epidemic.
the perception of fat content of foods is an important issue influencing subsequent food reward.
the perceived healthiness of food may influence subsequent eating behaviour and this is moderated by restrained eating.
